identity.name: Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom
native_names: Kūšān šahr (Middle Persian, 'domain of the Kushans')

land.text: the western half of the Kushan realm under Sasanian governors titled Kushanshah: Bactria, Sogdia and the Kabul valley

predecessors.note: The same kingdom: the Kushano-Sasanian page says 'Established: c. 230 CE'; Cliopatria draws its first thirty years (238-259) as the Western Kushans row and changes the row name in 260. The western-kushans dossier draws 226-259, so this dossier starts in 260 to avoid drawing the land twice.

land.text: the Peshawar valley (Gandhara), the 184 cells Cliopatria moves from the Eastern Kushans to the Indo-Sasanian shape in 260

predecessors.note: Gandhara, the farthest eastward extent of the kingdom on its page, passes from the Eastern Kushans in Cliopatria's 260 shape (the eastern-kushans dossier carries the matching loss).

land.text: the northern part: Bactria and Sogdia, the 1,437 of 1,438 cells of Cliopatria's Kidarite shape of 358 that lie inside the Indo-Sasanian shape of 357

successors.note: Around 360 (page decade 360-370; infobox c. 365): 'lost much of their domains to the invading Kidarites'. The kidarites dossier calls this predecessor 'kushano-sasanian-kingdom'; the slug that exists is indo-sasanian-empire.

rulers.title: Kushanshah (coins: Kushanshahanshah)

rulers.title: Kushanshah
rulers.note: Reigned 330-365 on the list; the strip stops at the 360 end of the state. In the second phase of his reign he had to introduce the Kidarite tamga on his coins (Kidarites page).

keyframe_review.note: 0.75 M km2 (Bactria, Sogdia, the Kabul valley and the Peshawar valley). The infobox gives no area ('Area: Not in source'), so the sanity check is by extent only: the page names 'Sogdia, Bactria and Gandhara' (captured 'following a series of wars in 225 CE') and Shapur I's Naqsh-e Rostam list ('the Domain of the Kushan up to the limits of Paškabur and up to Kash, Sughd, and Chachestan', Shapur I page). The shape is the Western Kushans of 238-259 (684,686 km2) plus the Peshawar valley. Mint towns Herat and Merv lie in the Sasanian Empire's own shape, not here.

Same outline (750,432 km2). Within it: Hormizd I Kushanshah's rebellion of 277-286 failed (no border change), and 'Around 325, Shapur II was directly in charge of the southern part of the territory, while in the north the Kushanshahs maintained their rule' (Kushano-Sasanian page): Cliopatria does not split the south off until 358 and the sasanian-empire dossier takes it in 358, so the shape stands; the page does not say which cells the 'southern part' was. Re-read 2026-10-19 (Peroz II Kushanshah page): it has no sentence for 325 and names no southern cities; it says 'the Sasanian King of Kings Shapur II (r. 309-379) incorporated Gandhara and Kabul into his own domains' after Peroz II (reign 303-330) and that Shapur II 'issued his own coinage from Kabul' (both undated). The south, Gandhara and Kabul, passes to Shapur II some time after c. 330 on that page and by 'around 325' on the Kushano-Sasanian page; no year is firm, so the shape and the 358 loss stand.

Same outline. Cliopatria's Gupta shape of 347 (Samudragupta) shares no cell with it (checked: 0); the pages opened are silent on any Gupta-Kushano-Sasanian contact. From about 350 'Shapur II gained the upper hand against the Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom during war', recorded as the contested south in the ledger (350-358).

Same outline until 357. Ammianus puts Shapur II's winter quarters on the eastern border in 356 and the treaty with the Chionites and Gelani in 358; the south is the contested zone 350-358 in the ledger and leaves the kingdom in 358.

correction.text: The north: Bactria and Sogdia, where 'in the north the Kushanshahs maintained their rule' until the Kidarites came around 360 (infobox end c. 365)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 358-360: Cliopatria's row ends in 357, but the pages date the end of the kingdom to c. 360-370 and the Kidarites to 'around 360'. From 358 the southern part passes to the Sasanian Empire ('Around 350, Shapur II regained the upper hand and took large territories in present-day Afghanistan and Pakistan. The Kushano-Sasanians still ruled in the north'), leaving the north, which equals Cliopatria's Kidarite shape of 358. The kingdom is drawn to 360, when the Kidarites dossier takes Bactria.

region.text: Balkh and the old Kushan west: Bactria, Sogdia and the Kabul valley

ledger.note: 260: the Kushano-Sasanian kingdom, Kushanshahs of Sasanian blood ruling the old Kushan west from Balkh, is drawn as its own state. The page: 'Established: c. 230 CE' with Ardashir I Kushanshah (230-245) and Peroz I (245-275); Ardashir I extended Sasanian rule into Bactria 'around 230 CE'. 260 is only Cliopatria's year (the Western Kushans row of 238-259 becomes the Indo-Sasanian row); the page is silent on any event in 260. Re-checked 2026-10-19 (thin item): the Ka'ba-ye Zartosht page has no entry on the Kushans and no date for 260, and the Kushano-Sasanian page never mentions 260 or a split between the Western Kushans and the Kushano-Sasanians, so as far as the pages go nothing happened in 260 and the western-kushans/indo-sasanian division is only Cliopatria's row change.

region.text: the Peshawar valley (Gandhara), the 184 cells Cliopatria moves from the Eastern Kushans to the Indo-Sasanian shape in 260

ledger.note: 260: Gandhara, the Peshawar valley, is drawn Kushano-Sasanian. under Shapur I (240-270) the Sasanians went 'further to the eastern parts of their empire in western Pakistan'; 'The farthest extent of the Kushano-Sasanians to the east appears to have been Gandhara', apparently not across the Indus. The page gives the reign, not the year; 260 is Cliopatria's year (Shapur I page: he burned Begram and Taxila in 262 and claimed land 'all the way to Peshawar'). Re-read 2026-10-19 (thin item): the Gandhara page gives no year for Sasanian or Kushano-Sasanian control (its only third-century Sasanian date is Sakastan, c. 224/5); the Peroz II Kushanshah page has Peroz II (reign 303-330) as the last Kushano-Sasanian ruler to issue copper coins in Gandhara, which keeps Gandhara in the kingdom to about 330.

region.text: the whole kingdom: the old Western Kushan land under 'Persian vassals known as the Kushanshas' (Bactria, Sogdia, the Kabul valley and, in Cliopatria's 260 shape, the Peshawar valley)

ledger.note: 260: the kingdom is a Sasanian vassal from the dossier's first year. Kushan Empire page: 'The Sasanians deposed the Western dynasty and replaced them with Persian vassals known as the Kushanshas', the establishment of the Indo-Sasanians or Kushanshas dated 'from around AD 240'; the Kushano-Sasanian page: they are 'sometimes considered as forming a "sub-kingdom" inside the Sasanian Empire', ruled by Sasanian princes titled Kushanshah (Ardashir I, Peroz I, ...) with their own capital, coinage and ruler list. The page's date (c. 240) falls before the dossier's start (Cliopatria's 260, see /ledger/0), so the relation is already running when the dossier opens; the region is the whole 260 shape (a reading). Mirrors sasanian-empire /ledger/23 (vassal_start 260, confidence 2). [Added after review me-06-d, 2026-10-19; Kushan Empire page re-read the same day]

region.text: the southern part of the Indo-Sasanian shape: the Hindu Kush side, the Kabul valley and Gandhara (about 1,148 of 2,585 cells); the Kushan Empire page, paraphrased: Shapur II took large territories in present-day Afghanistan and Pakistan

The page does not name the ground fought over; the zone is the southern part that the Kushan Empire page says he took.

The year 358 is the end of the war (Shapur II page) and Cliopatria's year; the Sasanian side (a Sasanian mint 'south of the Hindu Kush' in 'the last phase of the reign') is undated on the page.

ledger.note: 360: Bactria falls to the Kidarites. 'It is thought that they were in firm possession of the region of Bactria by 360'; 'In 360-370 CE, a Kidarite kingdom was established in Central Asian regions previously ruled by the Sasanian Empire' and 'replaced the Kushano-Sasanids' (Shapur II page: Bactria lost 'around 360 CE'; Kushano-Sasanian page: 'lost much of their domains' to the Kidarites). The page gives the decade 360-370 and the infobox c. 365; 360 is the earliest of them and the year the kidarites dossier founds the Kidarite state.

Kushan Empire page: 'In 360 a Kidarite Hun named Kidara overthrew the Kushano-Sasanians and remnants of the old Kushan dynasty'; after Shapur II's gains around 350 'The Kushano-Sasanian still ruled in the north', and 'They probably maintained control until the rise of the Kidarites under their ruler Kidara'. The south leaves the vassal kingdom already in 358, through the loss to sasanian-empire above (direct Sasanian land from then). sasanian-empire /ledger/39 ends its vassal tint in 358 over the whole shape; the north stays a vassal to 360 here, so that event should move to 360 over the north (request to me-06-c; the Osroene/Adiabene dossiers of me-06-b close their client relations with the loss in the same way). wars.name: Shapur I's campaigns against the Kushans

zones.text: Peshawar and Gandhara, 'all the way to Peshawar'

wars.outcome: Shapur 'annexed most of the land of the Kushans' and conquered Khwarezm in 242; in 262 he 'burned the Kushan cities of Begram and Taxila'. His inscription claims the Kushan domain up to Paskabur, Kash, Sughd and Chachestan. The Sasanians appear not to have crossed the Indus (Kushano-Sasanian page).
wars.note: The Kushano-Sasanian page places the capture of Sogdia, Bactria and Gandhara in 225 and the extension into Bactria around 230 under Ardashir I; the Shapur I page does not mention the Kushanshahs. [Reviewer me-06-d, 2026-10-19: clipped from 241-262 to the kingdom's life (starts 260); the campaigns of 241-259 fall in the western-kushans years]

wars.name: Rebellion of Hormizd I Kushanshah
wars.outcome: Hormizd I Kushanshah, whose coins use the title Kushanshahanshah, rebelled against Bahram II and failed (Kushano-Sasanian page); the Kushan Empire page says, in paraphrase, that he rebelled against the Sasanian Empire while keeping Kushan titles and coinage.
wars.note: The page's text dates the revolt 277-286, its list gives Hormizd I as Kushanshah 275-300. No territory is said to have changed hands, so the zone is empty and the land is not drawn contested.

notes:
Written by me-06-d on 2026-10-19 from five pages (the page budget for 4 shapes). The infobox of the Kushano-Sasanian page gives no area, so no area comparison could be made.

ONE STATE OR TWO WITH THE SASANIANS: Cliopatria's Indo-Sasanian Empire (260-357) shares Wikidata Q1661685 with the Sasanian Empire, but the page calls the kingdom 'sometimes considered' a sub-kingdom inside the Sasanian Empire, ruled by Sasanian princes titled Kushanshah, with its own capital (Balkh), coinage and ruler list. It is therefore a different state: a dependency of the sasanian-empire dossier (which records the vassal relation as vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart indo-sasanian-empire), not a merge. The display name is the Wikipedia title; 'Indo-Sasanian Empire' is the Cliopatria name.

START AND THE WESTERN KUSHANS: the page dates the kingdom c. 230 (infobox) or 225 (lead). Cliopatria draws 238-259 as the Western Kushans row, every cell of which lies inside the 260 shape, and the western-kushans dossier (sa-02) draws 226-259 with this dossier as its successor. To avoid drawing the land twice this dossier starts in 260 (found event at confidence 1: the page is silent on 260). The colour agent should give western-kushans and indo-sasanian-empire one line (both family persia); the orchestrator may merge them into one dossier covering c. 230-360.

END: the page gives c. 365 (infobox), 360-370 (text), 'around 360' (Shapur II), 360-370 (Kidarites). The dossier ends in 360 so that the kidarites dossier (founded 360) takes Bactria without an overlap; Cliopatria's Kidarites row begins in 358 and its row for this state ends in 357. In 358 the south goes to the Sasanian Empire (matching the sasanian-empire dossier's gain of 358), leaving the north for 358-360 (new keyframe). The kidarites dossier names its predecessor 'kushano-sasanian-kingdom' (no such dossier): it should read indo-sasanian-empire.

UNSETTLED: (1) 'Around 325, Shapur II was directly in charge of the southern part of the territory': the page does not say which cells; Cliopatria and the sasanian-empire dossier keep the south Kushano-Sasanian until 358, and so does this one. (2) Gandhara: the Kushano-Sasanian page gives it to the Sasanians in 225 or in Shapur I's reign, the Kushan Empire page has the Little Kushans in the Punjab from Taxila after 270; Cliopatria moves 184 Peshawar-valley cells in 260, and the ledger follows it (confidence 1). (3) No Gupta contact: Samudragupta's conquests of the Kushan remnant (the Gupta Empire row begins its large shape in 347) are not on any page opened here. (4) The Kushanshahs' dates disagree on the page itself (Ardashir I 230-245 against 233-245; Hormizd I 275-300 against a revolt 277-286). (5) The Chionites of Ammianus are not shown to be the Kidarites; the Kidarites page says they are 'likely' the same nomads (Shapur II page).

COUNTERPARTS: chionites (Grumbates, Ammianus; not a Cliopatria row) is named in one war; no dossier requested because the Kidarites dossier covers the people.

REPAIR 2026-10-19 (author, after review me-06-d): (1) Added vassal_start 260 and vassal_end 360 with counterpart sasanian-empire (the reviewer's blocking finding; Kushan Empire page re-read: 'Persian vassals known as the Kushanshas', 'from around AD 240'; 'In 360 a Kidarite Hun named Kidara overthrew the Kushano-Sasanians'). The south leaves the vassal state in 358 through the loss event; only the north is a vassal to 360. sasanian-empire (me-06-c) ends its tint in 358 over the whole shape: ask me-06-c to move /ledger/39 to 360 over the north. (2) Thin items tried, none dated: the Ka'ba-ye Zartosht page is silent on the Kushans; the Gandhara page gives no year for Sasanian control; the Peroz II Kushanshah page has no 325 sentence and says only that Shapur II incorporated Gandhara and Kabul after Peroz II (reign 303-330), undated. The shape and the 358 loss stand. (3) The two war entries clipped by the reviewer (/wars/0 from 260, /wars/3 to 360) were left as the reviewer set them.
